tagline: Complex AI. Explained visually. Built practically.
title: AI Automation vs Traditional Automation
disclosure: Fictional teaching scenario. Wouri Express and its people are invented; the setting draws on documented conditions in Douala, Cameroon.

onScreen.text: “If delivered, send the SMS.” That is automation.
onScreen.emphasis: “Read what the driver wrote and decide.” That needs AI.

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: Delivery marked done? Send the customer an SMS. Wouri Express automated that years ago, with no AI at all.

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: Read what the driver wrote and decide what it means: that needs AI. This last lesson is about knowing which is which.

onScreen.title: AI Automation vs Traditional Automation
onScreen.subtitle: AI Fundamentals · Lesson 10 · The whole Friday pipeline at Wouri Express, Douala

messages.text: Mbella: A vendor says I should replace all my automation with AI. Even the SMS. Should I?
Mbella: The SMS has worked every day for three years. Why would I touch it?

ui.title: Ndedi's list
lines: Reading driver notes: slow by hand, wrong by rule
Sending SMS: a rule, never fails

lines.speaker: amara
lines.text: A vendor told Mbella to replace all her automation with AI, Tanyi. Even the SMS that has worked for three years.

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: Ndedi's list says it better. Driver notes: wrong by rule, slow by hand. SMS: a rule, never fails. Refunds: a person.

left.title: Traditional automation
items: Fixed rules, same input, same output
Structured data: a status, a number

right.title: AI automation
items: Learned judgment, can vary between runs
Handles what no rule could list

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: Traditional automation follows fixed rules. Same input, same output, every time. Cheap, fast, easy to test.

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: AI automation uses learned judgment. It reads messy text and photos, handles cases no rule could list, and can vary between runs.

lines.speaker: gatekeeper
lines.text: Money, deletion, safety: rules with a human click. Reading and drafting: AI. Never the other way around.

onScreen.title: Rules around the AI, not instead of it

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: Here is the Friday pipeline we built across this series. The schedule and the export are rules. Plain code.

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: Reading the notes and drafting the sentences are AI. That is where judgment is needed. The citation check is code.

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: And the send is a person. Rules around the AI, not instead of it. Each part does what it is best at.

items.text: Paste the sheet's numbers into the draft
Sort each note into a cause, with a quote
Suggest what to change next week
Refunds and discounts: a person, always

lines.speaker: kito
lines.text: I label every step. Schedule, export, pasting numbers, the delivered SMS: rules. Same way every time.

lines.speaker: amara
lines.text: Sorting notes and writing sentences: AI. And the vendor's idea of replacing the SMS with AI?

lines.speaker: kito
lines.text: No. A rule that never fails stays a rule. AI goes where a rule cannot read the input. People keep every decision with money in it.

items.text: Fixed cause list: port, road, customer, other, not stated
Ten example notes with the right answer in the skill
Fifty test notes run every week; drift is reported

lines.speaker: hallucinator
lines.text: Gate locked, came back at four. Customer. Or other. Or road. Each run I feel differently. Variety is creativity.

lines.speaker: kito
lines.text: Not in a pipeline. I fix the cause list, add ten worked examples to the skill, and run fifty test notes weekly. Forty-nine matched.

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: AI automation can vary between runs. So surround it with rules: a fixed list, examples, weekly tests, a pause if the score drops.

ui.subject: Re: replacing our automation with AI
body: Thank you. Our SMS rule stays; it has never failed.
We use AI where a rule cannot read the input: driver notes and report drafts.
Refunds and schedule changes stay with people.

ui.title: Friday pipeline, week 41: send the report?
summary: Rules ran, AI steps tested, 49 of 50

lines.speaker: kito
lines.text: Mbella writes back. The SMS rule stays. AI reads the notes and drafts. People keep refunds and schedule changes.

lines.speaker: gatekeeper
lines.text: Week forty-one runs: rules, then AI, then Ndedi's click. That click is the most important automation she never automated.

items.label: Accounting
items.text: Rule: match invoice totals. AI: read the supplier's email. Person: pay

items.label: Clinic
items.text: Rule: send reminders. AI: sort patient messages. Person: diagnose

items.label: Recruiting
items.text: Rule: check required documents. AI: summarise CVs. Person: hire

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: Same three labels anywhere. Rule: match totals, send reminders, check documents. AI: read emails, sort messages, summarise CVs. Person: pay, diagnose, hire.

onScreen.title: Who owns this?
items: Wouri Express owns the pipeline, the rules and the tests
Ndedi maintains the skill and the example notes
The AI provider can be swapped; the rules stay
Accountable: the person whose click sends

lines.speaker: gatekeeper
lines.text: The company owns the pipeline, rules and tests. Ndedi maintains the skill. The provider can be swapped. Whoever clicks send is accountable.

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: Ten lessons, one company, one Friday report. Rules for the predictable, AI for the messy, people for the consequences. That is the foundation.

onScreen.title: Your build challenge
items: Label each step: rule, AI, or person
Keep the click with a person

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: Your challenge: take one process at work and label each step: rule, AI, or person. Then build only the AI steps.

onScreen.cta: End of AI Fundamentals · Next: Building AI Employees

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: Don't just use AI. Build it to work reliably. That was AI Fundamentals. Next series: building AI employees.
